What makes it different

Built for staying with content, not just generating from it.

  1. Content made easier to enter

    Before anything else, Omphalis brings the source in cleanly. Each kind of content (articles, PDFs, EPUBs, Word docs, podcasts, videos) runs through its own extraction pipeline: clutter removed, layout untangled, transcripts cleaned, long-form made readable. Comprehension starts before any note appears.

    Omphalis does not only analyze content. It makes content easier to enter.

  2. The shape, not the gist

    Most tools reduce a piece to an answer. Omphalis shows its shape first: sections, argument flow, transitions, dense moments, claims, evidence, and the places worth re-entering.

    A summary gives you the gist. Omphalis gives you the shape.

  3. A companion, not an afterthought

    Omphalis stays with you while you read, listen, watch, or work through a PDF, not only after you upload. It lives close to the moment of attention, where understanding actually happens.

    A companion for the content itself, close to where attention happens, not a detour you take after the reading is already behind you.

  4. Your marks, kept as meaning

    When you mark a paragraph or a timestamp as important, confusing, worth using, or worth questioning, that mark is a first-class object. It records what mattered to you, not what a model guessed mattered.

    Omphalis preserves what you noticed, not just what a model summarized.

  5. Connections from what you chose

    Threads grow from the moments you marked, not generic similarity between files. A newer piece can pick up an idea you marked before, or challenge one you held, or join a line of thought you are already developing.

    Omphalis connects the moments you chose, not just the documents you uploaded.

Omphalis gives long content a clean page, a clear map, and a margin for what matters.

  1. Arrives clean. It strips away the noise. Any source: articles, podcasts, PDFs, videos. Clutter falls away, and what is left is readable.
  2. Shows its shape. It reveals the shape. Typed moments, so you see the argument before you read a word of it.
  3. Marks the hard parts. It explains what you might miss. Sparse notes where they earn their place. Hover one to read it.
  4. You keep what matters. You keep what matters. Click a line to keep it. That mark is yours, and it is the whole loop.
  5. Connects over time. And it connects what you keep. Your marked moment meets the things you saved months ago.

Omphalis remembers what you marked and where. When you come back to that topic later, it’s there.

You can add a note. You don’t have to. A tap is enough.

Omphalis prepares the path. You decide what matters.

Not another chat box for your files.

Most tools like this are used one way: to get the gist and move on. You ask, it answers, and the thing you saved you never really read. It feels efficient, and it builds nothing that stays.

Omphalis is built the other way around. It starts with the content itself: its structure, its dense moments, the places where your attention should sit. When it helps, the help sends you back into the source, not around it. Maps and marks, not shortcuts.

Not a summarizer. Not a way to skip what you saved. Not a second brain that asks you to think for it.

Works with the content you already use.

Omphalis does not need to own the content. It helps you understand and mark what you already read, watch, or save.

Newsletters, your own notes, and voice notes flow through the same pipeline. Subscribe to Substack or any publication with a feed right in your Inbox, alongside your podcasts.

Ask your whole library, get sources back.

Open one panel from anywhere to jump to a source in a keystroke, or ask a real question. Answers are drawn only from what you have kept, and every claim returns to the source it came from.

Memory

Omphalis keeps a small, structured memory of the topics you return to and what you have already grasped, so it can choose better moments to show you next. Every entry is visible in Settings, and you can remove any of them.
